title: John Cage & I-Ching
content_html:
John Cage & I-Ching

SELECT I Ching outcomes, map to parameters
CHANGE Charts, iterations, layering by chance
RECONSTRUCT Score / print emerges from operations

Cage maps I Ching outcomes to musical and visual parameters via charts and grids. Chance procedures drive selection and transformation; works emerge as reconstructions of these operations. I Ching coin tosses pick values from charts (8×8 = 64 fields), which Cage mapped to musical or visual parameters. Iterative throws apply to successive decisions: ordering fragments, densities, coordinates, layers, colors, or radio settings. The process mutates structure. The final score/print is the visible trace of chance operations + material constraints, reconstructed by performance, printing, or viewing context.

John Cage Selected Works

  • Music of Changes (1951) composed via I Ching chance operations; charts for sounds, durations, dynamics, tempi, densities.
  • Imaginary Landscape No. 4 (1951) uses chance to govern radio parameters; method parallels Music of Changes.
  • Cage’s visual art at Crown Point Press used I Ching-based coordinates for placement, layers, and colors; includes the Ryoanji series.
